prompt:
A wind turbine operates in two successive stages. The turbine blades extract kinetic energy from the wind with an efficiency of 45% (0.45). The electrical generator converts the mechanical energy from the blades into electrical energy with an efficiency of 88% (0.88).
(a) Calculate the overall efficiency of the wind turbine system. [1]
(b) Explain why the overall efficiency is less than the efficiency of either individual stage. [1]
answer:
(a) 40% (or 39.6% / 0.40)
(b) Each stage dissipates energy, so the second stage operates on only a fraction of the original input energy, compounding the losses.

mark_scheme.criterion: (b) explains that energy is dissipated at each stage OR the second stage only receives a fraction of the total initial energy

hints: In (a), multiply the two decimal efficiencies together.
In (b), think about what each stage loses to thermal stores.
solution:
(a) Overall efficiency eta_overall = eta_blades * eta_gen = 0.45 * 0.88 = 0.396 approx 40% (or 39.6%).
(b) Each stage inevitably dissipates some energy as heat and sound. Because the generator receives only the reduced energy delivered by the blades (45%), its losses are compounded, resulting in an overall output that is a smaller fraction of the initial wind energy than either stage alone.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (b) tests qualitative reasoning about sequential energy degradation.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored as an original two-part drill on compound stage efficiencies.
